reef.name: Lingcod & rockfish
reef.life_stage: Adult lingcod and recreationally targeted rockfish; rockfish species occupy different niches.
reef.habitat: Rock relief, connected rough ground and sand–reef edges are search leads. A high terrain score measures structure, not abundance.
reef.method: Sounder first, then a controlled bottom drift with your double-drop rig. For lingcod, investigate ledges and edges; for rockfish, also inspect suspended marks above the reef. Reset when bottom contact or boat control deteriorates.
reef.timing: Seasonal nesting and species movements can change use of the reef. Do not turn a spawning season into an assumed bite window.
reef.condition_response: Wind, chop and opposing seas reduce rig control. Surface radar/model currents help plan a test drift; the boat’s observed track and line angle determine the actual setup.
evidence_needed: Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.search_for: Search mapped rock relief and rock–sediment boundaries; inspect both the bottom and schools suspended above it.
reef.presentation: Use a controlled bottom drift for lingcod, and adjust the rig to the depth of identified rockfish marks. Reset when line angle prevents effective contact.
reef.caution: Rockfish species have different niches and restrictions; a terrain grade is not a catch probability.
required_to_confirm: Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.life_stage: Coastal fish targeted by recreational anglers; nursery and trawl samples are distinct evidence.
halibut.habitat: Work connected sediment habitat and its edges. The current map’s shallow sediment areas are research candidates, not confirmed concentrations.
halibut.method: Search an area with a controlled drift and a presentation near the seabed. Use the sounder to check the edge and bait; move between comparable depth bands when an area produces no evidence.
halibut.timing: CDFW describes shallow spawning movements, but the calendar cannot locate fish. Local prey, visibility and present conditions remain important.
halibut.condition_response: Enough movement to cover ground can help searching, but excessive drift makes near-bottom presentation difficult. No universal current-speed optimum is assigned.
evidence_needed: Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.search_for: Start on mapped shallow sand or mud, especially where bait occurs near a bottom transition.
halibut.presentation: Keep bait or a lure near the bottom on a controlled drift; change depth or location when bait and bottom contact are absent.
halibut.caution: Bottom temperature and current are not measured by the surface layer; confirm the actual depth with sonar.
required_to_confirm: Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.life_stage: Ocean-feeding fish; species and stock identification affect legal access.
salmon.habitat: Mobile forage and water-column habitat matter more than a fixed reef pin. Coastal search sectors are geographic references.
salmon.method: Check the current local season, then use lawful gear to search observed bait and fish marks at their actual depth. Separate trolling presentation depth from seabed depth.
salmon.timing: Run timing and prey vary among years. Old landing reports or a moon phase do not establish today’s school position.
salmon.condition_response: Evaluate the outbound and return sea directions, trolling control and fog. Temperature or chlorophyll can guide a search only when recent, quality-screened and supported by forage evidence.
salmon.search_for: Use recent legal-season forage and identified fish observations to choose coastal feeding water.
salmon.presentation: Use lawful trolling gear at observed bait and fish depth, checking the entire transit and return forecast.
salmon.caution: No fixed reef or modeled surface temperature establishes an active salmon school.
salmon.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.life_stage: Surface-oriented fish encountered by West Coast troll fisheries; size and behavior vary.
albacore.habitat: Recent fronts and water masses can narrow an offshore search. Clouds, coarse pixels and stale imagery weaken the inference.
albacore.method: Compare recent SST, chlorophyll and current context, then look for actual bait, birds or fish. Start a search sector only after a fuel, range and return-weather plan; a colored front is not a catch location.
albacore.timing: Migrations change through the season and among years. Do not keep a fixed offshore hotspot alive after its supporting observation ages out.
albacore.condition_response: Longer exposure and a deteriorating return matter for the Parker. The comfort view and ensemble uncertainty apply to the complete travel window, not just the troll.
evidence_needed: Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.search_for: Prioritize ocean fronts and water transitions as search context for surface-oriented juveniles; look for forage and identified fish.
albacore.presentation: Use a searching troll or present bait at confirmed activity; compare both sides of a water transition rather than committing to a temperature number.
albacore.caution: Adult deep-water habitat and juvenile surface fisheries are different; fronts alone cannot confirm albacore.
required_to_confirm: Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
albacore.thermal_note: Broad juvenile eastern-Pacific tagged-fish envelope from the reviewed HMS synthesis, not an optimum.

bluefin.name: Pacific bluefin tuna
bluefin.life_stage: Mobile fish with size-dependent behavior and depth use.
bluefin.habitat: Schools can move quickly and occupy different depths. A single SST band is not a universal optimum.
bluefin.method: Treat offshore sectors as search references; use fresh school and bait evidence, appropriate equipment and lawful technique. Actual sonar marks should guide presentation depth.
bluefin.timing: Dated sightings can lose value rapidly. A past fleet track or landing count does not establish a current school.
bluefin.condition_response: Use the full trip exposure and return forecast. Surface-current products cannot predict a school’s movement or a deep jig’s drift.
evidence_needed: Recent identified school locations and observation method
Search effort and outcomes, not only successful reports
bluefin.search_for: Inspect ocean water transitions together with recent identified tuna and bait observations; check multiple depths.
bluefin.presentation: Use sonar and current school depth to choose live bait, a casting or vertical jig, or trolling. Match tackle to the fish size rather than the mapped water temperature.
bluefin.caution: A broad temperature range is not a bluefin bite curve; a surface map can miss deep schools.
required_to_confirm: Recent identified school locations and observation method
Search effort and outcomes, not only successful reports
bluefin.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.life_stage: Adult-sized crabs; juvenile nursery habitat cannot be treated as a harvest hotspot.
dungeness.habitat: Broad, depth-qualified sediment areas are starting hypotheses. Crab distribution, predation, molt, bait and gear all affect results.
dungeness.method: When the season and chosen gear are permitted, compare a small number of sediment locations with consistent bait, gear and soak effort. Record empty sets as well as catches. Check bottom type and retrieval conditions before setting.
dungeness.timing: Season permission, health restrictions and trap permission are checked separately. Molt and local movement may change availability.
dungeness.condition_response: Longer/deeper sets increase handling, buoy-line and retrieval demands. The user’s 200-ft ceiling stays in force. A deeper comparison requires new depth-qualified habitat, lawful gear and a suitable retrieval plan.
evidence_needed: Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.search_for: Search mapped sand and mud in a legal area and season, comparing depth and soak effort systematically.
dungeness.presentation: Use lawful crab gear suited to the actual depth and retrieve safely; log soak duration, bait, depth and empty sets.
dungeness.caution: Neither sea-otter presence nor deeper water alone establishes productive crab grounds.
required_to_confirm: Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
